text:
Josh Norris has played 20 games this season, and for a center whose last few years have been interrupted by injuries, that's worth noting first. The Sabres acquired him from Ottawa in the March 2025 trade for Dylan Cozens, and his line so far reads a quiet four goals and seven points, with his ice time drifting down to 13:31 a night over his last ten (as low as 9:13 against Los Angeles). He snapped a six-game goal drought with two against Columbus on Nov. 6, and "Just Be a Threat" was how the team's video framed his mindset.

The points undersell him. The Sabres have scored 11.2 fewer goals than their chances deserve with Norris on the ice, one of the biggest gaps in the league, and that has cost him assists. His own finishing is right where it should be (four goals on 4.07 expected goals, a measure of chance quality), and Buffalo outplays opponents at five-on-five in his minutes, with 52% of the expected goals. His top skating speed sits in the 94th percentile. If the luck around him evens out, the production should look much more like the player Buffalo traded for.
